chapter: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
title: Vic Dickenson, Bobby Darin and who had hit records
summary: Tangent on 'Please Don't Talk About Me', Darin's 'Mack the Knife' and Hampton having no hit.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I still love that number. Do you know every time I see Vic Dickerson, I ask him to play that for me. That's one of my favorite tunes, and I just love to hear Vic Dickerson play it with the plunger.
Oh yeah, "Please Don't Talk About Me When I'm Gone." He plays oh in a groove (Singing) "Please don't talk about me when I'm gone ....."

(Humming) ... the way Vic ... boy I said I could hear him play that all night long. Every time I see him, I say, Vic play "Please Don't Talk About Me When I'm Gone." The same way we were talking today about Barry--
No about .... what's his name? Sang 'Mack the Knife.' White guy.
Darin, greatest one I ever heard. He beats Louie with feeling on 'Mack the Knife,' I thought. Bobby Darrin is the only one that had that feeling on 'Mack the Knife.'
That was a big hit for him.
Yes it was. That Louie sang it well, but Bobby Darin sold more records than Louie on 'Mack the Knife.' Yeah.
Louie never had a tremendous hit until 'Dolly,' right?
No, 'Hello Dolly,' not really. Lionel has never had a hit.
Do you remember Lionel ever having a hit record?
Closest thing he probably did was 'Flying Home.' And that's really not a--that's a jazz hit but not a popular hit.
Lionel's a big name, super star, out there today, never had a hit.
